title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: bounded single-processor rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the strictly-bounded single-processor attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^127.80 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) and solves z=g^a by serial van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point Pollard rho on the cyclic group GT of prime order r, with a HARD global charged-work cutoff W_max=ceil(1.25*k0) multiplications (k0=sqrt(2*r*ln(1/0.61))) checked before every multiplication, so all walk and restart multiplications are inside W_max. theta=2^-30; segments reaching 2^38 multiplications without a distinguished point are truncated, and the expected number of truncations over the whole budget is ~2^-271 (so with overwhelming probability none occur and no collision opportunity is lost). Distinguished points are stored as 384-bit fingerprints with (A,B); birthday false matches over <=2^100 records are ~2^-185 and are resolved by recomputation (continuing on a false match). The bounded success probability is at least 1-0.61^1.5625 minus exceptional losses (truncation ~2^-271, single-processor detection lag <=2^38/W_max ~2^-89.7, fingerprint ~2^-185), i.e. >= 0.39, under the random-mapping heuristic, supported by a strictly-bounded toy experiment. The total-work score is independent of the processor count. Peak memory is bounded hard by a fixed 2^100-slot table (record count mean 2^97.74, Chernoff): at most 2^108 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^32 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps; generic square-root accounting, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Strictly-bounded single-processor serial-VW distinguished-point rho on a prime-order-l subgroup of F_q^* (cyclic, standing in for GT). Enforces the hard cutoff W_max=ceil(1.25*k0) before every multiplication (reports strictly_bounded_ok and the max observed multiplication count), counts walk and restart multiplications, truncates long segments, and reports the fraction of trials finding a usable collision within W_max plus mean truncations. Toy-scale evidence for the random-mapping collision-time model and the bounded algorithm only; the toy stores exact group elements (production uses 384-bit fingerprints with resolution).
